description: What the work VMs (vtnet2, 10.10.60.0/24) and the leased VMs (vtnet5, 10.10.90.0/24) are doing, from the firewall's filter log, state counters, resolver log and Suricata alerts in Loki, and from the hypervisor's view of each guest. The alerts in rules-tenant.yaml each point at a panel here. Wiring, and what these logs do not cover: security/docs/wiring, section 3.

panels.description: How full the firewall's pf state table is: states in use over the table size, highest value in the last 5 minutes. A full table refuses new connections on every segment, not just the one that filled it. Yellow at 50% and red at 80%, where Firewall State Table Over 50% and Over 80% fire. No data means no pfstats lines are arriving; Firewall Stats Stopped covers that.

targets.expr: max(max_over_time({job="pfstats"} | regexp "\\bstates=(?P<v>[0-9]+)" | unwrap v [5m])) / max(max_over_time({job="pfstats"} | regexp "\\bstates_max=(?P<v>[0-9]+)" | unwrap v [5m]))

panels.title: State Table Used

panels.description: Sources in the firewall's virusprot table right now. A source that exceeds its connection-rate limit is banned for up to an hour, which cuts that VM off. Anything above zero fires Firewall Banned a Source.
panels.title: Banned Sources

panels.description: Times pf refused a state in the selected range: the per-source limit (src_limit_hits) and the state limit (state_limit_hits). The counters are cumulative, so each figure is how much the counter grew in the range; a firewall reboot inside the range, which restarts the counter, is not counted. Fires Firewall Per-Source Limit Hit and Firewall State Limit Hit over the last 10 minutes.
panels.title: Limit Hits, Selected Range

panels.description: Suricata alerts on the selected segment's interface in the range, from the syslog EVE output (alerts only). The Suricata Alerts dashboard has the signature and SID filters. A severity 1 alert on the lease interface fires Suricata Alert on Lease Segment (critical); 3 or more of any severity in 10 minutes fires Suricata Alerts on Lease Segment (lower severity); 5 or more in 10 minutes on the work interface fires Suricata Alerts on Work Segment.
panels.title: Suricata Alerts, Selected Segment

panels.description: The pf state table's fill level over time, highest value in a rolling 5 minutes. Dashed lines mark 50% and 80%, the thresholds of the two Firewall State Table alerts.

targets.expr: max(max_over_time({job="pfstats"} | regexp "\\bstates=(?P<v>[0-9]+)" | unwrap v [5m])) / max(max_over_time({job="pfstats"} | regexp "\\bstates_max=(?P<v>[0-9]+)" | unwrap v [5m]))

panels.title: State Table Usage

panels.description: Per-source and state limit hits in a rolling 10 minutes (growth of the cumulative counter; a firewall reboot is not counted), and the number of banned sources. All three should sit at zero. Alerts: Firewall Per-Source Limit Hit, Firewall State Limit Hit and Firewall Banned a Source.
panels.title: Limit Hits and Banned Sources

panels.description: New flows the firewall let through (passed) and refused (blocked) per minute, for the selected segment. The pass rules on the work and lease interfaces log, so a flow they pass is one line and lines track flows; traffic inside a tenant's own Tailscale tunnel is one flow to a relay or peer. The dashed line is 3000 a minute, where Tenant New Flow Rate High fires after 5 minutes. A blocked series that climbs while the passed one is flat is a VM running into a deny rule. Lines from a banned source are rate-limited at ingest, so the blocked series understates a ban.
panels.title: New Flows per Minute

panels.description: Packets per second through the firewall's lease (vtnet5) and work (vtnet2) interfaces, in the firewall's direction: in is what the VMs send. Both segments always show; the Segment picker does not apply. Alerts at 15000 in for the lease segment (75% of one lease's ceiling of 20000 packets/s) and 50000 in for the work segment, each for 5 minutes (Lease Segment Packet Rate High, Work Segment Packet Rate High). A single lease cannot exceed its own ceiling; see Packets Dropped by the Lease Limit for the exact per-guest count.
panels.title: Interface Packet Rates

panels.description: What each guest sends, read from the hypervisor's side of its virtual NIC (the host's receive counter on the tap device), averaged over 5 minutes and named by roles/pve_guest_metrics. Only guests on the tenant and lease bridges (vmbr2 and vmbr5) are listed, so the firewall VM and other infrastructure are not; the Guest picker narrows it and the Segment picker does not apply. Dashed lines: 10 MB/s, where Guest Sending Over 10 MB/s fires (15 minute average), and the lease cap of 12.5 MB/s.

targets.expr: sum by (host, guest, nic) (rate(node_network_receive_bytes_total{device=~"tap[0-9]+i[0-9]+"}[5m]) * on (host, device) group_left (guest, nic) fleet_pve_guest_nic_info{bridge=~"vmbr(2|5)",guest=~"$guest"})

panels.title: Egress per Guest

panels.description: Conntrack entries the hypervisor holds for each tenant or lease source address (fleet_pve_tenant_conntrack_entries). The dashed line is 20000, where Tenant VM Conntrack Entries High fires after 10 minutes. Empty until the pve_guest_metrics role writes the series.
panels.title: Conntrack Entries per Tenant VM

panels.description: Packets per second each leased VM's packet-rate ceiling dropped, per guest, averaged over 15 minutes (fleet_pve_tenant_policed_packets_total, a counter that resets when the VM restarts). The window is 15 minutes because the exporter writes a new value every 5 minutes, so a shorter one can hold none and read 0. A VM at its ceiling (20000 packets/s) shows here and nowhere else exact: the segment rate cannot name it. The dashed line is 100 packets/s, where Lease Packet Limit Reached fires after 5 minutes. Empty means no lease is being limited, or the series is not written yet.
panels.title: Packets Dropped by the Lease Limit

panels.description: 1 while a running lease has its packet-rate police filter, 0 when it lost it (Proxmox's hot NIC update deletes the filter). A line at 0 is a lease with no packet-rate ceiling: Lease Packet Limit Missing fires after 10 minutes. Empty is normal when no lease is running.
panels.title: Lease Packet Limit Active

panels.description: 1 while the Proxmox firewall is filtering a tenant or lease VM, 0 when it is not (fleet_pve_tenant_firewall_active). It is 1 only when the datacenter firewall is on, the VM has firewall=1 on net0, its .fw file has enable: 1 and the right GROUP, and its tap chain exists. A line at 0 is a VM with no ipfilter, macfilter or tenant and lease group rules: Tenant Firewall Not Filtering fires after 10 minutes. Empty is normal when no tenant VM is running.
panels.title: Tenant Firewall Active

panels.description: Seconds since the Proxmox guest exporter (fleet-pve-guests, every 5 minutes) last completed a run. If a read fails it keeps the previous file, so the series above look fine while old; this age is how that shows. Yellow past 10 minutes, red past 20, where Proxmox Guest Exporter Stale fires after 5 more. No data means the role is not deployed on this host.
panels.title: Guest Exporter Age

panels.description: Where the selected segment's new flows went: destination address, port and protocol, most flows first, passed IPv4 flows only. Read from the firewall's filter log, so the address is what the VM asked for, before NAT. Many destinations on one port is a scan; one destination and one port is a flood or a retry loop. Traffic inside a tenant's own Tailscale tunnel, or through their exit node, is one flow to a Tailscale relay or peer here, not the inner destinations.
panels.title: Top Destinations by Flow Count

panels.description: Which VM opened the new flows: the source address (the VM's own address, the filter log is before NAT) and its interface, most flows first, passed IPv4 flows only. The 10.10.60 addresses are work VMs, the 10.10.90 addresses are lease VMs. Counts flows the firewall saw: a tunnel inside the VM is one flow, not the flows inside it.
panels.title: Flows by VM

panels.description: Suricata alerts in the range for the selected segment, per interface (in_iface) and signature. Only alerts reach Loki; TLS server names and HTTP hosts stay in the firewall's local eve.json. The Suricata Alerts dashboard has the SID filter and the raw alert.
panels.title: Suricata Alerts by Interface and Signature

panels.description: The names the work and lease clients asked Unbound for in the range, most asked first (query lines only, not replies). Both segments always show; the Segment picker does not apply because Unbound logs the client address, not the interface. Only plain DNS on port 53 reaches Unbound: DNS over HTTPS, and DNS inside a tenant's own Tailscale tunnel, are not visible here, DNS over TLS (TCP 853) is blocked on the lease segment only, and DNS over QUIC (UDP 853) is being blocked there. Random-looking names are malware; one name repeated is a broken client.

targets.expr: topk(20, sum by (name) (count_over_time({job="unbound"} | regexp `info: (?P<client>10\.10\.(?:60|90)\.[0-9]+) (?P<name>[^ ]+) (?P<qtype>[A-Z0-9]+) IN\s*$` | client!="" [$__range])))

panels.title: Top DNS Names

panels.description: Queries per client address over time (10.10.60 work, 10.10.90 lease), the interval chosen by the time range. A client far above its neighbours is the one to look at. Plain DNS on port 53 only; encrypted DNS and DNS inside a Tailscale tunnel do not appear.
panels.title: DNS Queries per Client

panels.description: Replies saying the name does not exist, per client address. A burst is a domain-generation algorithm or a client in a retry loop. Tenant DNS NXDOMAIN Storm fires above 300 in 5 minutes across both segments.
panels.title: NXDOMAIN Replies per Client

panels.description: What the Proxmox firewall dropped, by rule chain: GROUP-tenant and GROUP-lease are the work and lease VM groups, in and out; a per-VM chain is a policy drop. Tailscale's UDP 41641 probing, benign and constant from the work VM, is left out. Proxmox logs at most one line a second per rule, so counts understate the attempts. An IN chain counts packets TO that VM, which another guest can cause, so only the OUT chains feed the alerts. Empty means nothing was dropped. Alerts: Tenant VM Probing Private Addresses and Tenant VM Attempted SMTP.
panels.title: Blocked Attempts by Chain

panels.description: Dropped packets in the range per chain and guest. vmid is the guest's Proxmox ID, read from the tap device in the log line; Guest Traffic or the Proxmox UI names it. For an IN chain it is the VM receiving the dropped packet, not the sender. DPT=25 lines in a GROUP-tenant-OUT or GROUP-lease-OUT chain are SMTP attempts.
panels.title: Blocked Attempts by Chain and VM

panels.description: The exact count behind the log lines above: packets the Proxmox firewall dropped per rule (smtp, private, private_in) in the preceding 15 minutes, from fleet_pve_firewall_dropped_packets_total, summed over IPv4 and IPv6. Not rate-limited like the log. The exporter writes a new value every 5 minutes, so a shorter window can hold none and read 0. Tenant SMTP Drops Counted fires on any increase of the smtp rule. Empty until the pve_guest_metrics role writes the series.
panels.title: Proxmox Firewall Drops by Rule

panels.description: The newest filter log lines for the selected segment, passes and blocks: interface, action, source to destination and protocol. A line that is not IPv4 shows the raw log line instead. Lines from a banned source are rate-limited at ingest, and a tunnel inside the VM is one flow. Expand a line for every label.
panels.title: Recent Flows

list.description: Which firewall interface the flow, alert and log panels follow. DNS, the Proxmox firewall panels, packet rates and per-guest panels always show every tenant.
list.label: Segment
list.name: segment
list.query: Work VMs : vtnet2, Lease VMs : vtnet5

title: Tenant Activity
